subject.title: Ensure transcript-to-client delivery consistency for channel-scoped sessions

question: What durable delivery-state contract should OpenClaw add for channel-scoped assistant transcript entries: a transcript-entry ledger, an extension of delivery_queue_entries, or a separate session-state projection?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable schema, adapter reconciliation API, idempotent redelivery policy, and Control UI/API status shape are cross-cutting product and compatibility decisions.

options.title: Design core receipt ledger first
options.body: Define a core SQLite delivery receipt table/API and Control UI state model, then implement adapter-specific reconciliation against that contract.

options.title: Limit To Queue Mitigations
options.body: Keep this issue open but only accept narrow recovery mitigations until maintainers are ready to commit to the broader delivery-state surface.

options.title: Split UI From Runtime Ledger
options.body: Create separate maintainer-owned runtime-ledger and Control UI follow-up items if the full design is too large for one implementation lane.

recommendation.title: Design core receipt ledger first
recommendation.body: Define a core SQLite delivery receipt table/API and Control UI state model, then implement adapter-specific reconciliation against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main ownership signal is the merged SQLite delivery queue and outbound recovery history that the receipt ledger would likely extend.
